children: After ditching phone mirroring to get drivers to use its native software, General Motors
is giving new Chevy Silverado and GMC Sierra truck owners a way to integrate Apple’s CarPlay
into the infotainment system without giving up screen space for its own software.

from its EVs three years ago in an effort to take full control of its in-car software and collect driver data that apps like CarPlay and Android Auto do not provide to the car manufacturer. It also provides car manufacturers like GM
an additional revenue stream through app subscriptions with their own vehicle software.
But starting with the newest models of the Silverado and Sierra, GM
is giving owners a new way to connect their phones to the vehicle’s native software.
By using picture-in-picture phone mirroring, GM

engineers have found a way to give drivers the option to use phone projection while at the same time keeping GM’s native software front and center. Now, CarPlay and Android Auto occupy a contextual card rather than use an entire screen.

“I think we’re landing in a spot where we don’t have a customer who has to decide, 'Oh, I’m going to use projection or I want to use the native system.' That’s our sweet spot,” said GM’s group product manager for Google built-in projection, Colin McCormick, to The Verge.

title: General Motors makes room for CarPlay and Android Auto in 2027 Silverado, Sierra
